english.title: Holder of on-premises licence fail to inform Commission of high turnover bingo period - Gambling Act 2005
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being the holder of an on-premises alcohol licence and not holding a bingo operating licence, failed without reasonable excuse to inform the Gambling Commission as soon as reasonably practicable about the beginning of a high turnover bingo period
english.legislation: Contrary to section 281(7) and (8) of the Gambling Act 2005.

english.notes:
(i) Section 281(2) of the Gambling Act 2005 provides that bingo played on premises in any period of seven days is high turnover bingo if
(a) the aggregate of stakes at bingo played during the period in the course of the activities of the club or institute exceeds £2,000, OR
(b) the aggregate of prizes at bingo played during the period in the course of the activities of the club or institute exceeds £2,000.
(ii) Section 281(3) of the Gambling Act 2005 provides that a high turnover period beings in relation to premises at the end of a period of seven days during which
(a) the aggregate of stakes at bingo played in the course of the activities of the club or institute exceeds £2,000, OR
(b) the aggregate of prizes at bingo played in the course of the activities of the club or institute exceeds £2,000.
(iii) Section 278 of the Gambling Act 2005 provides that the offence applies to certain alcohol licensed premises only.
(iii) See also the offence of providing facilities for gambling under section 33, see offence wording GA05001/H8180.
